name: Packets identification
purpose: pid maps the source packets produced by the spacecraft, or by ground systems, to SCOS-2000 telemetry packet identifiers. The telemetry packetiser recognises a packet by its APID, PUS type and subtype and up to two extra identification fields (PI1, PI2) whose position pic gives. It looks up pid with that 5-field key and then files and distributes the packet under the processing keys found there: the SPID, which selects the fixed layout in plf, and the TPSD, which selects the variable layout in vpd. One packet may be processed both ways. Packets identified by APID alone use 0 for the other key fields. Since R5.0 each distinct packet must have its own SPID. Duplicate keys are allowed only with PID_VALID selecting one valid record. Once archiving has started, the key-to-SPID allocation and the TPSD should not change and archived SPIDs must not be deleted, or retrieval services such as GDDS break. Internally generated packets (UDC, MISC, synthetic, system control) should also have pid and tpcf entries, with an unused type/subtype/APID combination. The table also sets the event packets raised on reception, the presence of a time field and of a checksum, and the period used for parameter expiry.

fields.name: PID_TYPE
fields.description: PUS service type of the TM source packet, an integer from 0 to 255. Zero means that the packet has no specific type, e.g. it has no PUS data field header.

fields.name: PID_STYPE
fields.description: PUS service subtype of the TM source packet, an integer from 0 to 255. Zero means that the packet has no specific subtype (e.g. no PUS data field header).

fields.name: PID_APID
fields.description: Application process identifier of the TM source packet: 0 to 2047 for source packets generated by the spacecraft, 2048 to 65535 for any other SCOS-2000 TM packet, such as packets generated by SCOS-2000 applications or by other control domains (e.g. SCOE equipment).

fields.name: PID_PI1_VAL
fields.description: Value of the first additional identification field (for example a structure ID or task ID), used together with APID, type and subtype to identify the packet structure; where and how wide the field is comes from pic. Unsigned integer from 0 to 2^31-1. Enter 0 when pic is not used for the packet, because the packetiser then searches pid with PI1 = 0 and PI2 = 0.

fields.name: PID_PI2_VAL
fields.description: Value of the second additional identification field (for example a function ID), used together with APID, type, subtype and PI1 to identify the packet structure. Unsigned integer from 0 to 2^31-1; enter 0 when pic is not used.

fields.name: PID_SPID
fields.description: SCOS-2000 Telemetry Packet Number (SCOS-2000 Packet ID, SPID). It uniquely identifies the structure of fixed TM packets described in plf and is the identifier used by tpcf, grpk and the archive; in releases up to S2K-R5 it also selected the history file in which the packet was archived. Unsigned integer from 1 to 2^32-1 (zero not allowed).

fields.name: PID_DESCR
fields.description: Textual description of the telemetry packet. When the packet triggers a SCOS-2000 event packet (PID_EVENT not 'N'), the packetiser uses this text as the event message.

fields.name: PID_UNIT
fields.description: On-board subsystem, intended for grouping packets for filtering (future extension). Grey and italic row in the ICD: not used and not currently supported by SCOS-2000.

fields.name: PID_TPSD
fields.description: SCOS-2000 Telemetry Packet Structure Definition, used only by the Variable Packets Display application. Set it to -1 for packets not described in vpd; otherwise give the structure identifier, an unsigned integer from 1 to 2^31-1 (zero not allowed), that VPD_TPSD uses. The TPSD of packets already in the archive must not be changed, or archived packets will be reprocessed incorrectly with a new database version.

fields.name: PID_DFHSIZE
fields.description: Start reference, in octets from the end of the SCOS-2000 packet header, for interpreting variable packets with vpd. With the SCOS-2000 packetiser the whole source packet is stored in the SCOS-2000 packet body, so the reference is the start of the source packet header plus this number of bytes, typically the source packet header plus the PUS data field header. Irrelevant for fixed packets (PID_TPSD = -1). Integer from 0 to 99.

fields.name: PID_TIME
fields.description: Whether the TM source packet contains a packet generation time field.

fields.name: PID_INTER
fields.description: Generation interval of periodic TM packets in milliseconds. SCOS-2000 uses it, plus a global margin, to decide when the parameter samples of a periodic packet expire, i.e. become invalid because no new packet arrived (pcf remark, p. 40). Must be left null for non-periodic packets.

fields.name: PID_VALID
fields.description: Whether this key combination is valid. It selects which SPID to use when several records share the same key. At import, if several records with the same key are flagged 'Y', only the last one stays valid and the others are forced to 'N'.

fields.name: PID_CHECK
fields.description: Whether the TM source packet carries a Packet Error Control field (checksum) and whether and how the packetiser checks it on reception. Missions may add options for other checksum algorithms.

values.meaning: Do not check the Packet Error Control field (absent, or check disabled for this packet)
Check the Packet Error Control field with the CRC specified in the PUS standard [RD-6]

fields.name: PID_EVENT
fields.description: Whether the packetiser generates a SCOS-2000 event packet when this source packet is received, and with which severity, e.g. to alert operators to anomaly reports. The event message text is PID_DESCR.

fields.name: PID_EVID
fields.description: Event number used as event ID of the generated SCOS-2000 event packet; the full event ID is 'TPKT_OBE::nnnn' with nnnn this value. A specific ID makes it possible to control the recipients of the event or trigger actions on reception. To avoid clashes with events of other SCOS-2000 applications (which use 5-digit numbers from 10000), values between 1 and 9999 are suggested. Optional; relevant only when PID_EVENT is not 'N'.

relationships.note: SPID identifies the fixed packet layout (plf), its characteristics (tpcf) and packet-group membership.
Variable packet structure used by the Variable Packets Display.
pic tells the packetiser where to read PI1/PI2 before searching pid.
Parameters in periodic packets expire after PID_INTER plus a global margin.

history: ICD 5.1 (p. 38-42) already has the 16 fields in this order (its table misnumbers PID_EVID as 15). It allowed several keys to map to the same SPID, and PID_SPID also selected the history file. ICD 6.0 widened the PID_SPID range from 2^31-1 to 2^32-1 (DCR-2421, ICD 7.0 Annex 1, p. 246). ICD 6.1 updated the PID_PI1_VAL/PID_PI2_VAL descriptions (CRY-OG-655 / DCR 3398, p. 251). ICD 6.4 stated that packets without a data field header can be recognised by APID alone (p. 255). ICD 6.5 (R5.0) deprecated mapping different packets to the same SPID and clarified the use of pid fields (DCR-3398, p. 256-257). The layout is unchanged in ICD 6.7 Draft A (p. 77-85), 6.9 (p. 80-89) and 7.0 (p. 82-91). pyscos2000 (ICD 7.2) matches: the same 16 fields and defaults, with the 6 key fields PID_TYPE to PID_SPID.

fields.name: PID_DESCR
examples: Amount of event identifiers not in line with N parameter
A data expected as float is Not a number (Nan)

notes: No structural discrepancy between ICD 7.0 and pyscos2000. ICD 7.0 marks PID_SPID with '*' (key) although the text says the packetiser key is the first five fields, so the import key is effectively type/subtype/APID/PI1/PI2 plus SPID. Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16: 11,150 packets, SPID range 101 to 1,000,006, all SPIDs unique. PID_UNIT, PID_INTER and PID_EVID are never filled, so Solar Orbiter relies on no periodic-packet expiry and on default event IDs. PID_TIME is 'Y' for 11,141 packets. PID_CHECK is 1 for only 6 packets. PID_VALID is 'Y' or empty (default 'Y'). PID_EVENT: A 6,360, I 1,374, W 1,159, N 1,095, empty 1,162. 2,063 packets have a TPSD (each TPSD used by exactly one packet, all present in vpd) and DFHSIZE 16; packets with TPSD -1 have DFHSIZE 16, 6 or 0. A 16-byte DFHSIZE matches the 6-byte packet primary header plus a 10-byte PUS data field header (inference from the values; the header layout is not in this table). No packet is described in both plf and vpd, and 31 fixed packets have no plf entry. Eleven packets have type and subtype 0, including three ground frame-quality pseudo-packets 'Bad/Idle/Good complete transfer frame' (APID 1, SPIDs 1000002/3/6), all with the same key 0/0/1/0/0 and PID_VALID 'Y'. Per the ICD only the last imported of these would stay valid. APIDs 2048-2065 are used for internally generated 'LMS_NNO/CEB/MLG' packets (ground station telemetry, consistent with the reserved NNO/CEB/MLG names in pcf).
